Chapter 1 • 3-Page Executive Strategy

Product Strategy Write-Up: AuraWardrobe AI

Building a Next-Generation Fashion Commerce Operating System for India

1 Step 1: Choose a Segment — Who We Are Building For

The Specific Segment: Urban Young Working Professionals & Couples (Ages 23–30) residing in Tier-1 Indian Metros (Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi-NCR, Hyderabad, Pune).

  • Demographics: Salaried corporate, tech, and creative professionals with annual personal income between ₹8L and ₹25L; monthly apparel spend ₹5,000–₹18,000.
  • Lifestyle Context: Fast-paced hybrid work weeks (3 days office, 2 days remote), active social calendars (weekend dining, rooftop cocktail mixers, cafe working), and frequent cultural/festive family commitments (pujas, weddings, sangeets).
  • Core Paradox ("Closet Saturation vs. Style Scarcity"): They possess overflowing wardrobes (40–80 garments), yet experience acute daily decision fatigue ("I have an overflowing cupboard but nothing to wear"). They shop monthly across Myntra, Ajio, Zara, Snitch, and Amazon, but endure high sizing variance, 34% return friction, and wardrobe color imbalance (e.g. 65% dark blue/black saturation).
  • Why this segment first? High disposable income, high digital fluency, camera-first mobile habits, and high willingness to adopt camera/AI tools to eliminate shopping friction.

2 Step 2: Map the 5 Gaps with Real User Evidence

Gap 1: Sizing Roulette & Return Friction

30–40% return rate across Indian D2C and Western brands. A "Large" in Snitch is 40" chest, while Zara's "L" is 44" and FabIndia regular ease is +3 inches. Users order multiple sizes, tying up capital in refund cycles.

Gap 2: Cognitive Overload & Decision Fatigue

Standard Indian portals bombard users with 50,000 algorithmic tiles. Endless scrolling causes high bounce rates, decision paralysis, and impulse checkout remorse.

Gap 3: Wardrobe Blindspots & Redundant Buys

Shoppers lack a digital inventory of what they already own. They repeatedly buy comfortable dark neutrals (e.g. 6 navy polos) while lacking essential bridge pieces (warm sand overshirts, light palazzos).

Gap 4: Social-to-Commerce Translation Friction

High Instagram/YouTube Reel inspiration vs. tedious multi-app hunting. Users spend 45 minutes manually searching for pieces from an influencer's reel with zero fit confidence.

User Voice Snippets:
"I have six navy blue polos and four black tees because I default to safe dark colors when in a hurry. When I needed to go to a family temple puja, I had literally zero traditional footwear to go with my kurta." — Aditya, 26, Bengaluru
"I see amazing styling reels on Instagram—like a cropped Kashmiri embroidered shrug over palazzos. But trying to find those exact pieces on Myntra or Ajio is exhausting. Also 90% of my pants are black because I'm terrified white palazzos will look awkward on my 5'3" frame." — Ananya, 25, Bengaluru

3 Step 3: Why Current Incumbents Have Not Solved Them

1. The GMV & Ad-Revenue Conflict of Interest: Incumbent platforms monetize through sponsored ads and transaction volume. An engine that tells the user "You already own 4 dark polos; do not buy this one" directly reduces immediate transaction GMV and ad impressions.
2. The "Blind Closet" Limitation: Platforms only know what a user ordered on their specific store. If a user bought their jeans at a Levi's store and their kurta on FabIndia, Myntra operates in complete blindness.
3. Subsidized Reverse Logistics Inertia: Incumbents treated 35% returns as an unavoidable customer acquisition tax, passing costs onto seller take-rates rather than eliminating pattern discrepancy at the source.

4 Step 4: Three Strategic Bets & Chosen Bet

Bet 1 • No AI

Concierge Capsule Trunk

Physical stylist sends 6 pre-measured garments monthly; user tries at home and keeps what fits.

Unscalable CapEx & logistics risk.
CHOSEN Bet 2 • AI-Led

AuraWardrobe AI

Computer vision closet audit + cross-brand anthropometric sizing + rationalized Shop for Me engine.

Zero inventory liability; software margins.
Bet 3 • New Business Model

Closet Equity Swap

Deposit unworn branded clothes for liquid credits to spend strictly on verified wardrobe gap items.

High warehouse grading complexity.

6 Step 6: Plan the First 30 Days (GTM, Risks & Metrics)

Days 1–10: Hyperlocal co-working activation (WeWork, BHIVE in Bengaluru); onboard first 30 tech professionals via 3-minute closet audit.
Days 11–20: "Closet Declutter & Gap Challenge" via WhatsApp/Instagram; reach 50 active users via organic word-of-mouth.
Days 21–30: Affiliate integration with Snitch, Rare Rabbit, and Myntra; achieve 100 power users with >= 1 strategic gap purchase.
North Star Metric Wardrobe Gap Conversion > 18%
Guardrail Metric Fit Return Rate < 8%
Kill Signal > 60% revert to search keywords
Chapter 2 • Prompt Engineering Note

Prompt Engineering Note (1 Page)

Top 5 critical prompts, 1 failed prompt post-mortem, and systematic AI output verification protocols.

Prompt 1: Multi-Subject Silhouette & Garment Deconstruction Vision AI 
"Analyze the 6 uploaded photos of Aditya and Ananya. Detect distinct individuals, separate multiple subjects in shared photos, and extract each garment item into a clean schema: Garment Name, Category, SubCategory, Cloth Type (weave & GSM), Wardrobe Type (occasion), Primary Color (with hex), Condition Score (1.0-10.0), Condition Label, Wear Frequency, Status (KEEP/REPLACE), Status Reason, and detected photo references."

Why written this way: Strict typed schema forces deterministic segmentation and eliminates hallucinated garment names, matching exact fabrics (pique cotton, slub linen, boucle fleece).

Prompt 2: Cross-Brand Pattern Sizing & Anthropometric Normalization Fit Engine 
"Write a deterministic algorithm `calculateBrandSizes(gender, chest, waist, height, armLength, inseam, bodyType)` that maps chest and waist inches to exact brand sizes across Snitch, Rare Rabbit, Zara India, Levi's, FabIndia/Manyavar, and Mango. Enforce brand-specific ease: D2C slim athletic cuts require +1 size for 40-inch chest, while ethnic kurtas allow 3 inches of traditional ease."

Why written this way: Eliminates static size charts. Models real pattern grading variations between Indian fast fashion and European cuts.

Prompt 3: Studio Flat-Lay Photorealistic Garment Generation Asset Matching 
"Generate high-end studio product flat-lay photographs on pure white seamless e-commerce background for the exact garments: 1. Men's deep navy blue pique cotton polo with ash grey collar and white tipping stripe. 2. Men's rose pink and cobalt blue buffalo check casual shirt. 3. Men's white camo marble polo with bright yellow placket lining. 4. Men's indigo slub linen mandarin short kurta. Top-down 90-degree flat lay perspective, soft natural contact shadows."

Why written this way: Ensures the inventory tiles match the exact clothes from the user's uploaded photos rather than generic stock photos.

Prompt 4: Three.js Real Facial Texture & Anatomical Mesh Mapping 3D WebGL 
"Mount a Three.js scene with a realistic human avatar. Load the real face photo texture using THREE.TextureLoader() onto a curved facial plane. Apply dynamic chest and waist scaling based on profile measurements. Connect torso and leg materials to live selected outfit state, and add an auto-spin toggle and fit tension heatmap."

Why written this way: Solved the user's feedback that the mannequin looked like a cartoon by grounding it in real facial texture and real body build.

Failed Prompt Post-Mortem 
FAILED: "Scrape Myntra for real-time inventory and pricing for polo shirts."

Why it failed: Modern Indian e-commerce sites employ strict Cloudflare anti-bot challenges and dynamic React hydration. Direct terminal curl or scraping returned 403 Forbidden.

How we resolved it: Replaced volatile live scraping with verified direct canonical URLs and grounded retail catalogs (Snitch, Myntra, FabIndia) with exact product IDs.

Output Verification Protocol
  • Terminal Sanity: Every build verified via npm run build (zero Rollup/Vite errors).
  • Network Check: Server verified via curl -I http://localhost:5173/ (HTTP 200 OK).
  • Mathematical Equilibrium: Verified that total outfit value = sum of pieces, and closet savings = sum of reused staples.
  • Visual Fidelity: Inspected generated studio images against the source photos to ensure 100% pattern and collar alignment.

Primary qualitative evidence grounding the problem statement in Tier-1 Indian Metro reality.

Interview 1: Aditya (26, Senior Software Engineer, Bengaluru)

Hybrid office worker (3 days office, 2 days remote); personal income ₹22 LPA; monthly fashion spend ₹8,000.

"Whenever I'm browsing in a hurry, I default to navy blue or black because I know it won't look weird. "Sizing is a nightmare: in Snitch I need an XL so the chest buttons don't gap, but in Zara an XL drowns me."

Interview 2: Ananya (25, Creative Brand Strategist, Bengaluru)

Chapter 5 • Prototype Walkthrough

Interactive Prototype Verification Guide

Step-by-step instructions for testing every component end-to-end.

1. Digitized Wardrobe Auditor & Studio Tiles

Switch profiles between Aditya and Ananya. Observe that cards feature only the studio-isolated garment matching the exact clothes in the photos. Click "📸 Worn in Photo" to view the original lifestyle photo in a lightbox modal. Click "🎽 3D Try On" to load that garment into the 3D studio.

2. 3D Virtual Try-On & Photorealistic AR Mirror

Toggle between the "Photorealistic Mirror" (displaying Aditya/Ananya's real face and body in studio lighting) and the "3D 360° Turntable" (orbiting Three.js mesh with facial texture mapping). Test the "360° Spin" and "Fit Heatmap" toggles.

3. Shop for Me (Personal Stylist)

Select an occasion (e.g., Tech Conference, Diwali Sangeet), slide the budget bar, and enter a styling intent. The engine calculates how much you save by reusing owned wardrobe staples (₹0 spend) and presents scrollable suggestion cards with direct "Buy on [Store]" product page links.

4. Reel Look Cloner with Multi-Frame Vision

Paste any Instagram Reel or YouTube Shorts URL (or click the 1-click sample links). Watch the 3-phase vision AI extract keyframes at 0:02, 0:06, and 0:12, identify closet synergies, and add the missing pieces to your cart with a 15% bundle discount.
